description: A single-panel Thermo-Calc (CALPHAD) calculation of the equilibrium phase fractions of the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C low-density steel as a function of temperature. The x-axis is Temperature (°C), running 600–1500 with major ticks every 100 °C; the y-axis is Fraction of Phase, 0.0–1.0 with ticks every 0.2. Four curves are labelled directly in the plot: L (liquid, upper right), γ (austenite), α (ferrite) and κ (κ-carbide). The α curve starts near 0.88 at 600 °C, falls steeply to a broad plateau of about 0.32 spanning roughly 900–1300 °C, then rises to about 0.7 near 1320 °C before falling abruptly. The γ curve leaves zero at about 600–650 °C, climbs to a wide plateau near 0.68 between about 900 and 1250 °C, then declines. The κ curve is a shallow hump peaking below 0.2 near 650 °C and returning to zero at a point marked by an arrow annotated "823°C". The L curve only appears above about 1350 °C, rising steeply to 1.0 at 1500 °C. The panel shows that austenite plus ferrite dominate over a wide high-temperature window, that κ-carbide is stable only below 823 °C, and that liquid forms only well above 1350 °C.

subfigures.description: Thermo-Calc phase-fraction vs temperature plot for Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C; x-axis Temperature (°C) 600–1500, y-axis Fraction of Phase 0.0–1.0; four labelled curves L, γ, α and κ. The κ curve goes to zero at an arrow labelled '823°C'.

observations.observation: The plot axes are x = Temperature (°C) from 600 to 1500 (major ticks every 100 °C) and y = Fraction of Phase from 0.0 to 1.0 (ticks every 0.2).
Four curves are labelled in the plot: L (liquid), γ (austenite), α (ferrite) and κ (κ-carbide).
The κ-carbide (κ) curve is a shallow hump that peaks below a fraction of 0.2 near 650 °C and falls to zero at the point indicated by the arrow annotated '823°C'.
The α (ferrite) curve begins near 0.88 at 600 °C, drops to a plateau of roughly 0.32 across about 900–1300 °C, then rises to about 0.7 near 1320 °C before falling sharply.
The γ (austenite) curve emerges from zero at about 600–650 °C and reaches a broad plateau near 0.68 between roughly 900 and 1250 °C before declining.
The L (liquid) curve only appears above about 1350 °C and rises steeply toward 1.0 at 1500 °C.
The caption states that these are fractions of the equilibrium phases (ferrite (α), austenite (γ) and κ-carbide (κ)) calculated by Thermo-Calc.
The caption text was used to identify the plotted curves; the image itself does not print the alloy composition or the database name.
The citing text states the phase diagram of the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel was calculated by Thermo-Calc with database TCFE7.
The citing text states κ-carbide appears by the eutectoid reaction γ → α + κ when the temperature falls below 823 °C, consistent with the arrow at 823 °C in the plot.
The citing text states that ferrite forms first during solidification and austenite forms by a peritectic reaction, and that the ferrite fraction reaches a minimum around 1000 °C.

The citing text notes a discrepancy between the Thermo-Calc equilibrium fractions and the fractions measured from the steel (non-equilibrium state; atomic vs. volume fraction), which the plotted curves alone cannot show.
